response: {"text":"The study examined how the formation of hydrogen gas bubbles influences the creation of tiny copper particles when an electric current is passed through a copper‑containing solution. It was found that the bubbles tend to merge and become larger, which in turn affects the uniformity of the particle sizes that are produced. Several variables that cause the size distribution to vary from run to run are also discussed. By applying a voltage that is just a little more negative than the level at which hydrogen starts to form, fine, branch‑like copper deposits can be grown on the negative electrode. However, the presence of hydrogen bubbles disrupts this growth, so preventing bubble formation is essential for obtaining a fine, consistent powder."}
